title: Data Flows and Colonial Regimes in Africa: A Critical Analysis of the Colonial Futurities Embedded in AI Recommendation Algorithms

bias_targets.methodology: Critical analysis and qualitative reflections from monthly discussions with Kenyan social media users, examining how Western-centric AI systems, data extraction, and recommendation algorithms marginalize African epistemologies and enforce colonial power dynamics.

Literature review and conceptual analysis of how facial recognition systems misclassify darker skin tones and how healthcare algorithms trained on Global North datasets fail to capture African realities, causing racial vulnerabilities.

Qualitative reflection on how social media recommendation algorithms and dominant AI systems reflect masculine worldviews, amplifying negative gender norms and stereotypes that disproportionately impact women in the African context.
Evaluation of natural language processing (NLP) systems' prioritization of colonial languages (e.g., English, French) over indigenous African languages, creating epistemic hierarchies and exclusion.
Case study analysis of algorithmically driven disinformation campaigns and psychographic microtargeting (e.g., Cambridge Analytica in the 2017 Kenyan elections) used to manipulate voter perceptions.

Reviewing existing algorithmic logic (such as using healthcare costs as a proxy for need) that inherently excludes poorer populations who spend less on healthcare despite having greater medical needs.
